scope: Phase 2 final 9 source-diagnostic Hays taxon records
nomenclature_conflict: Kew currently uses Lolium × boucheanum for L. perenne × L. rigidum; EPPO uses it for L. multiflorum × L. perenne, while USDA GRIN uses L. × hybridum for latter. Hold all hybrid ID until taxon concept resolved.

flora_treatment.source: Diggs et al. 1999 Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

reference_descriptions.description: Woody perennial spreads via rhizomes, forming dense bamboo colonies; old Flora stems 2–8 m.
Lower culm internodes often shortened and compressed; vital fishpole-bamboo feature.
Culm flattened or grooved on one side above branching nodes.
Usually two to three unequal branches at nodes.
Narrow lanceolate leaves often 5–15 cm, with small petiole; flowers uncommon.

taxa.prior_visual_notes: Woody running bamboo thicket, narrow lanceolate leaves and node branching, multiple culms; compatible with Phyllostachys.
taxa.prior_unverified: Basal culm internode crowding/compression characteristic of fishpole bamboo, grooved internodes and branch node details not demonstrated; planting or escaped-colony provenance not established.
taxa.lookalikes: Other Phyllostachys and native Arundinaria gigantea
taxa.next_proof: Expose lower culm nodes, internode compression, grooves and branches; document landscape planting versus spread.
taxa.hold: Cultivation/escaped colony and lower culm anatomy not verified.

flora_treatment.source: Diggs et al. 1999 Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

reference_descriptions.description: Huge perennial tussock, usually 2–3 m or more.
Long coarse leaves with sharp finely serrate margins.
Dense fringe of hairs approximately 3–5 mm.
Large multi-branched feathery panicle around 25–100 cm, not small cylindrical bottlebrush.
Multi-flowered spikelets; pistillate lemmas densely silky, staminate florets less hairy.

taxa.prior_visual_notes: Some tall, silvery plume-bearing ornamental clumps look consistent with pampas grass; narrow, strap-like leaves in tuft.
taxa.prior_unverified: At least one observation (62141431) shows multiple short cylindrical fountain-grass-like plumes that are NOT clearly the large branched Cortaderia panicle, raising a possible mixed/misidentified iNaturalist set. Cultivated landscaping likely.
taxa.lookalikes: Cortaderia jubata and Cenchrus setaceus fountain grass
taxa.next_proof: Recheck iNaturalist 62141431 for possible misidentification; compare entire branching plume, ligule and floret hairs.
taxa.hold: CRITICAL: some saved source photos resemble fountain grass and may be misidentified; likely planted.

flora_treatment.source: Diggs et al. 1999 Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

reference_descriptions.description: Annual coarse millet, cultivated or casual seed-spill volunteer.
Long hairs borne on papillae on sheaths.
Short ciliate membrane about 1–3 mm including hairs.
Rather dense branched panicle about 6–20 cm in Flora of North America.
Plump ripe spikelets 4–6 mm; lower glume about one-half to three-quarters of spikelet, upper many-veined.

taxa.prior_visual_notes: Green grain-bearing inflorescence, coarse grass-like blades and stem closeups visible; a separate full plant photographed in disturbed ground.
taxa.prior_unverified: Several views show unusually narrow/contracted green heads versus typically broad, loose proso millet panicle, which could reflect immaturity or incorrect ID; no ripe grain/spikelet morphology or cultivar origin verified.
taxa.lookalikes: Panicum capillare, P. dichotomiflorum, other seeded millets
taxa.next_proof: Measure ripe spikelet/glume and photograph hairy sheath from same plant; establish seed spill or spontaneous wild context.
taxa.hold: Narrow immature-looking heads in previous image sample; not species-verified or established.

flora_treatment.source: Diggs et al. 1999 Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

reference_descriptions.description: Densely tufted nonrhizomatous perennial, around 60–100 cm in old regional Flora.
Wide diffuse pink-purple head with hairlike branches and pedicels.
Firm membranous decurrent ligule approximately 1.8–5 mm in FNA.
Usually one-flowered about 3–5 mm; glumes notably shorter than lemmas.
Lemma may carry variable (2–)5–15 mm awn in old Flora; some FNA specimens awnless.

taxa.prior_visual_notes: One airy purple-pink muhly plume over dense basal tuft.
taxa.prior_unverified: Single image consistent with ornamental pink muhly, not species confirmation or wild population.
taxa.lookalikes: Muhlenbergia reverchonii, M. lindheimeri and horticultural pink muhly
taxa.next_proof: Separate glume and mature lemma with awn and inner ligule; check plant origin and possible cultivar.
taxa.hold: One prior ornamental-looking image; no verified wild Hays species identity.

flora_treatment.source: External modern species or hybrid reference

reference_descriptions.description: Annual or short-lived tufted perennial; lower stems may root at nodes.
Fluffy silvery-pink or purple panicle fading gray.
Ovate spikelet covered in reddish silky hairs several millimeters long.
Lower glume much smaller than often five-veined upper glume with narrow beak.
Short membrane about 0.5–1.4 mm under one botanical treatment.

taxa.prior_visual_notes: Characteristic pink fuzzy open plume-like seedheads and clumped foliage visible; strong general photo evidence.
taxa.prior_unverified: Scenes resemble ornamental or managed bunches; ligule and florets not resolved and independent wild established stand not shown.
taxa.next_proof: Photograph ripe isolated spikelet hairs, different glumes, collar and rooted Hays population.
taxa.hold: Pink heads visible but minute anatomy and independent naturalization not proven.

flora_treatment.source: External modern species or hybrid reference

reference_descriptions.description: Tightly tufted perennial 25–70 cm in GrassBase.
Threadlike or needlelike rolled blades about 0.4–0.5 mm across.
Membranous ligule 1.5–4 mm, not ciliate.
Narrow panicle with few spikelets; long hyaline glumes around 5–10.5 mm.
Hardened lemma 1.8–3.6 mm with long geniculate awn often 50–90 mm.

taxa.prior_visual_notes: Fine threadlike foliage and flowing pale feathery seedheads above tufted base; compatible with Mexican feathergrass.
taxa.prior_unverified: Could reflect planted ornamental Mexican feathergrass, and awns/lemma microcharacters are invisible.
taxa.next_proof: Measure entire bent awn, glumes and true ligule from same plant and document whether planted.
taxa.hold: Potential ornamental planting; earlier photos lack ripe spikelet microcharacters.

flora_treatment.source: External modern species or hybrid reference

reference_descriptions.description: Perennial densely tufted grass, culms about 20–130 cm.
Narrow rolled blue-green harsh blade with pronounced midrib.
Narrow cylindrical bottlebrush panicle around 6–30 cm.
Inner involucre bristles feathery, longest about 16–40 mm.
One to three spikelets within bristly unit, about 4.5–6.5 mm; lower glume tiny or absent.

taxa.lookalikes: Cenchrus ciliaris; other fountain grasses; Cortaderia
taxa.next_proof: Get original Hays whole-plant source photo and separate bristly spikelet unit plus glumes with rights checked.
taxa.hold: ZERO prior usable original source images; cannot visually confirm Hays plant or use source photos.

flora_treatment.source: External modern species or hybrid reference

reference_descriptions.description: POWO accepts L. × boucheanum but currently says parents are L. perenne × L. rigidum.
EPPO applies same name to L. multiflorum × L. perenne, a conflicting concept.
USDA GRIN treats multiflorum × perenne as L. × hybridum and flags × boucheanum auct. usage.
Awn, auricle and floret traits overlap among parental species; a lone ryegrass photo is not hybrid proof.
Single Hays observation remains unsupported by viewed source pixels and has no verified hybrid voucher.

taxa.lookalikes: Lolium perenne, L. rigidum, L. multiflorum and L. × hybridum
taxa.next_proof: Resolve conflicting hybrid name and parentage across authorities before checking same-plant spikelets, auricles and expert specimen/voucher determination.
taxa.hold: HARD TAXONOMY HOLD: one named hybrid, NOT a confirmed ordinary species and no photographs inspected.

flora_treatment.source: Diggs et al. 1999 Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

reference_descriptions.description: Large tufted/rhizomatous perennial about 1–3 m.
Pale central blade midrib and rough edges; some cultivated forms variegated.
Ciliate membrane about 1.5–3 mm in old regional Flora.
Large branched panicle 10–35 cm with ascending branches.
Paired stalked spikelets with long basal hair tuft, one short and one long pedicel.
Spikelets about 4–5.5 mm and twisted bent lemma awn about 5–10 mm in regional Flora.

taxa.prior_visual_notes: Clumped tall arching narrow leaves in an ornamental-looking garden setting.
taxa.prior_unverified: No panicle or spikelets; cannot verify species or wild occurrence.
taxa.next_proof: Find ripe paired silky spikelets and twisted awns with leaf midrib and collar; check landscape origin.
taxa.hold: Only one old photo of ornamental foliage, no verified spikelets or naturalized Hays stand.
